1. Hematite: This is the most common type of iron ore, comprising up to 70% of all iron ore reserves worldwide. It has a high iron content (around 60-70%) and is typically found in sedimentary rocks. Hematite is often used to produce pig iron, which is used in the production of steel.

2. Magnetite: This is another common type of iron ore, accounting for around 15-20% of global reserves. It has a higher iron content than hematite (around 70-80%) and is often found in igneous or metamorphic rocks. Magnetite is also used to produce pig iron, but it is more difficult to extract due to its magnetic properties.

3. Siderite: This is a less common type of iron ore, comprising only about 5% of global reserves. It has a lower iron content than hematite or magnetite (around 40-50%) and is often found in limestone or other carbonate rocks. Siderite is used to produce ferrous sulfide, which is used in the production of steel.

4. Taconite: This is a low-grade iron ore that contains less than 30% iron. It is often found in sedimentary rocks and is not as commonly used as other types of iron ore. Taconite is usually upgraded by removing impurities and concentrating the iron content before it can be used in steel production.

In addition to these primary iron ores, there are also secondary sources of iron such as recycled steel scrap, which can be melted down and reused to produce new steel products.
